own_solution.law: Q = (m/M)3R(T2-T1), using M = 0.2072 kg/mol. The base heat is 3.6112934 kJ. For additional heated lead of mass q, Q(q) = ((0.5+q)/0.2072)(3)(8.314)(60)/1000 kJ.
assumptions: Use the stated constant molar heat capacity of 3R throughout the temperature interval.
Lead added to the block shares its initial temperature and undergoes the full temperature increase.
Lead on the scale pan and lead used only in an earlier experiment do not participate in the present heating.
No heat is lost to the surroundings.

notes: All certified answers agree with the heat-capacity calculation. Added heated masses of 0.07, 0.18 and 0.52 kg give 4.11687, 4.91136 and 7.36704 kJ, respectively. Heater power changes the required duration, t = Q/P, and cancels from Pt at fixed temperature endpoints. The relations require the ordinary conversion of molar mass from g/mol to kg/mol and heat from J to kJ.
